EDITION AND COUNTING NOTES Chekhov: About Love and Other Stories is the specific Rosamund Bartlett selection recommended in S095. It represents a concrete book rather than an undefined “complete works.” The broad authors’ canon in S131 supports Chekhov’s stories generally, not that exact translated selection. His constituent stories are not ranked again separately. Gogol: Petersburg Tales means the familiar St Petersburg story grouping, including The Overcoat and The Nose. It is a collection/cycle entry, not a claim that all editions have identical contents. Neither story is counted again as a separate ranked work. The Overcoat essay is constituent-work evidence, not an independent poll of every possible anthology. [S038] Shalamov: Kolyma Stories is counted as the complete connected Kolyma undertaking, not as two separate books because of its English publication format. Donald Rayfield’s NYRB volumes are Kolyma Stories and Sketches of the Criminal World: Further Kolyma Stories. [S024, S065, S070] Sholokhov: the unit is the complete four-book Quiet Don. English editions can divide the novel differently, including the title The Don Flows Home to the Sea for later sections; the entry does not mean only the first half. [S166] Solzhenitsyn: The Gulag Archipelago is counted once as the complete multi-volume undertaking. In the First Circle refers to the complete version, not an assumption that the earlier shortened The First Circle has identical contents. Publication chronology differs among secondary summaries; the version distinction is the important point here. [S106, S215–S216] Pushkin: The Queen of Spades is ranked as the individual work, not a mixed anthology that also contains the five Tales of Belkin. This avoids counting the same stories twice. [S042, S095, S191] Krzhizhanovsky: Memories of the Future here means Joanne Turnbull’s seven-story English collection, not only its title story or an assertion that the selection was originally issued as one Russian-language volume. The comparative reviews in S075–S076 concern Autobiography of a Corpse, a different collection; they are not disguised reviews of Memories of the Future. [S063, S066, S075–S076] Paustovsky: the ranked reading unit is Books 1–3 as collected in Douglas Smith’s NYRB translation. The original autobiography extends to six books. This particular volume is not advertised here as the complete memoir. [S145] Ginzburg and Gorky: Journey into the Whirlwind and My Childhood refer to the named first volumes, not every subsequent volume of their autobiographical sequences. [S204–S207, S211–S212] Alternate titles: Moscow to the End of the Line is Moscow–Petushki; Buddha’s Little Finger is also published in English as The Clay Machine-Gun; A Sportsman’s Sketches is also known as Sketches from a Hunter’s Album. Transliterations and English titles vary across editions. [S017, S108, S150, S188] SOME CLOSE CALLS EXAMINED BUT NOT INCLUDED These are not a second ranking: The Luzhin Defense (Nabokov); The Norm (Sorokin); Home of the Gentry (Turgenev); Sevastopol Sketches (Tolstoy); The Blue Book (Zoshchenko); Evenings on a Farm near Dikanka (Gogol); Journey from St Petersburg to Moscow (Radishchev); Goat Song (Vaginov); Watermark (Brodsky); The Cathedral Clergy (Leskov); The Lower Depths (Gorky); Soul and Other Stories (Platonov); and Little Tragedies (Pushkin). Their omission reflects the 100-place limit and the priorities above, not a finding that they are minor works. [S157–S160, S179, S189, S194–S201] Several choices remain openly contestable.
